The joint rescue teams led by the Nepal Army have continued their search and rescue efforts on the ninth day on Thursday, with the number of missing people estimated at 4,875. The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, leaving a trail of destruction and thousands of people missing.

article_sentences: The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal has risen to 1,243, with thousands still missing as rescuers battle rain, debris and difficult terrain to search for survivors along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.

The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on 26 August, swept through towns and villages across northern and central Nepal, causing widespread destruction and leaving thousands unaccounted for.
According to Nepal Police, 4,875 people remain missing, including 583 foreigners.
Security forces have rescued 11,993 people by helicopter and overland routes, while more than 21,000 personnel have been deployed for search and rescue operations.
The disaster has hit eight districts particularly hard.
Chitwan has recorded 348 deaths, followed by Nawalparasi East with 218, Nawalparasi West with 208 and Nuwakot with 155.
Rasuwa has reported 127 deaths, while Gorkha, Dhading and Tanahu have recorded 69, 60 and 38 deaths respectively.
On the Chinese side of the border, the death toll from flooding in Tibet's Gyirong county has risen to 21, with another 541 people reported missing.
China's foreign ministry said nearly 100 Chinese nationals remain unaccounted for in Nepal.
Rescue efforts have intensified at hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, where hundreds of workers are feared trapped inside tunnels and underground powerhouses.

Data from Nepal's Independent Power Producers' Association shows 947 people from various hydropower projects remain unaccounted for, although authorities have yet to determine how many are trapped underground and how many were swept away.
More than 557 people are missing from the 216-MW Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project alone.

article_sentences: Actor Sonu Sood visited Nepal following the devastating floods that have caused widespread destruction in the country.
He arrived in Kathmandu with relief material and went to Trishuli Bazar on Wednesday, September 2, to understand the situation.
The actor spent time with local residents who are affected by the disaster and listened to their experiences.
His visit comes as rescue and recovery operations remain underway in several parts of Nepal.
Taking to his social media, he wrote, "Standing here today at the Trishuli River, where the floods have left behind unimaginable loss-broken homes, broken families, and lives changed forever.
Nepal is not alone.
I stand with its people, and I will do everything I can to bring hope, rebuild homes, and help families begin again."
Sonu also praised India's assistance, saying, "I hope that we are all able to bring some aid for the people of Nepal so that Nepal can again stand back on their feet.
I also think Indian government has done phenomenally...also thanks to our Prime Minister Mr. Narendra Modi...

the kind of help that has been provided to Nepal it's commendable and I think we should keep on continuing sending this aid because they need it and on the ground when I come when I meet those families I know that it's not going to get resolved in couple of weeks or months it's something that we have to keep on sending, continuing our support and I think that's the only way we can get them back to their normal lives," as quoted by ANI.

stories.headline: ‘Like God to Us’: Nepal Flood Survivors Thank India for Shelter, Medical Care
stories.title: ‘Like God to Us’: Nepal Flood Survivors Thank India for Shelter, Medical Care
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NUWAKOT (Nepal): Nepal Flood survivors in Nuwakot have found a crucial refuge at the Nepal-Bharat Maitri Bhawan, where an India-supported hospital is providing shelter, medical care and essential assistance to people displaced by the devastating flash floods that struck the district on August 26.
For many survivors, the facility has become more than a hospital.

Situated on relatively higher ground, the Maitri Bhawan has offered a safe place to stay for hundreds of people who lost their homes and belongings after the Bhote Koshi River floods wreaked havoc across Nuwakot and adjoining areas.
The building, which houses the Ayurveda and Alternative Hospital, was reconstructed with financial assistance from the Embassy of India following the 2015 earthquake.
Speaking to ANI, hospital chief Dr Narendra Prasad Giri said the facility opened its doors to displaced people who had nowhere else to go.
"This building is a post-earthquake reconstruction, and it was assisted financially by the Embassy of India.
This building is a core support for the people.
Many devastated people who were rescued from there, we brought them here and treated, and their health is now stable," Giri said.
He said more than 100 displaced people were staying at the facility every night, while medical assistance was also being extended to people housed in nearby holding centres.
"After the flood, around six people came to us by themselves, and they had minor cut injuries, that we had to do sutures.
And one had a tendon injury also, that we repaired the next day here," he said.
Giri said the hospital has deployed around 11 doctors, five to seven nurses and five to six paramedics.

stories.headline: SDM Cannot Halt Panchayat Samiti Chairman Election Over Horse-Trading Allegations: Himachal Pradesh High Court
stories.title: SDM Cannot Halt Panchayat Samiti Chairman Election Over Horse-Trading Allegations: Himachal Pradesh High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Himachal Pradesh High Court has held that a Sub-Divisional Magistrate cannot halt the election of Chairman and Vice-Chairman of a Panchayat Samiti on the ground that allegations of electoral irregularities or malpractices are pending police inquiry.

The Court termed the SDM's action in deferring the election as “wholly untenable, manifestly illegal and contrary to rule of law”, observing that such action lacked statutory backing and exceeded the powers conferred upon him as an Executive Magistrate.

Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua remarked that: “Sub Divisional Magistrate's action… to halt the election of Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the Panchayat Samiti, Indora… is wholly untenable, manifestly illegal and contrary to rule of law.
Such action lacks statutory backing.
It exceeds the power conferred upon him as an Executive Magistrate and transgresses the constitutional mandate.”
The petitioner, Ankush Indoria, was one of the 26 elected members of the Panchayat Samiti, Indora, District Kangra, following the Panchayati Raj elections held in May 2026.
Although all elected members took oath on June 8, 2026, the election for Chairman and Vice-Chairman was not conducted.
The petitioner approached the Himachal Pradesh High Court alleging that the authorities had failed to discharge their statutory duty to convene the election meeting.

The Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), Indora, justified the delay on the ground that a complaint alleging horse-trading, monetary inducements and attempts to influence the election was pending inquiry before the SDPO, Indora.

The High Court held that Section 79 of the Himachal Pradesh Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 mandates that the election of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman must be held immediately after the elected members take oath.
The Court clarified that although the seven-day timeline under Rule 85(1-A) of the Election Rules was subsequently omitted, the amendment did not alter the statutory mandate under Section 79.
The Court rejected the SDM's justification for deferring the election pending inquiry into allegations of horse-trading and monetary inducements.

stories.headline: MP Aga Ruhullah urges Budgam administration to reopen Yousmarg tourist resort
stories.title: MP Aga Ruhullah urges Budgam administration to reopen Yousmarg tourist resort
stories.summary: Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has urged the Budgam district administration to immediately reopen the tourist resort Yousmarg, citing severe economic distress faced by locals dependent on tourism for their survival. In a communication to the Deputy Commissioner of Budgam accessed by news agency KNS, the Lok Sabha member said a delegation of residents from Yousmarg had recently met him and expressed "serious concern" over the continued restrictions, especially when other tourist hotspots across the Union Territory are functioning normally. "The local residents expressed serious concern that when other major tourist destinations in Jammu & Kashmir are open and receiving visitors, Yousmarg should also be considered for reopening, subject to all necessary safety and administrative protocols," the MP said in his letter. Describing tourism as the "primary source of livelihood" for the area, MP Mehdi pointed out that pony operators, horse riders, hoteliers, shopkeepers, transporters and tour guides have been the worst hit by the prolonged curbs, with many families struggling to make ends meet. "In view of the above, I request your good office to kindly examine the matter on priority and take appropriate steps for reopening Yousmarg for tourists, if there are no prevailing security or administrative constraints," he wrote. He further appealed to the administration to give "due consideration" to the livelihood concerns of the local population while taking any decision. Yousmarg a tourist destination in central Kashmir's Budgam district remained largely inaccessible to tourists since security measures were tightened following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Although authorities had allowed limited movement earlier this year, the flow of visitors has remained negligible, dealing a crippling blow to the local economy. Notably, Local stakeholders have repeatedly demanded the removal of restrictions, warning that the continued shutdown could push many families into irreversible financial ruin.

article_sentences: "Doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed… Yet again," wrote Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on X, external, reacting to smart first quarter GDP data that came out earlier this week, widely beating forecasts, but also sparking a major controversy over its credibility.

On the face of it, the 7.8% number was a shot in the arm for the prime minister who's recently faced scathing student anger over his government's handling of exam paper leaks and rising youth unemployment.

While those longstanding concerns have not gone anywhere, the better-than-expected growth print suggests that his government may have deftly weathered the Middle East oil shock despite heavy dependencies on imported crude.

According to Sajjid Chinoy, chief India economist at JP Morgan, India's "cyclical growth recovery" had been visible for the past six months, driven by a huge fiscal stimulus, including direct tax cuts in February last year, a reduction of consumption taxes in September and interest rates which have come off by about 1.5% since early 2025.

"But the question was, could India insulate that recovery from events in the Middle East, and this is where the government deserves enormous credit," Mr Chinoy told India Today, external news channel, adding that the urgency with which Delhi diversified its energy imports in the face of the Hormuz blockade helped the country protect its growth.

What also helped Asia's third largest economy power ahead amid the disruption in global energy markets was a strong acceleration in exports and a surge in private corporate investments, which has long been a point of great concern for economists.
Exports grew by a sharp 12% despite tariff uncertainties on the back of strong global demand and a weak exchange rate.
Economists reckon a 15% slump in the Indian rupee against the US dollar may have helped companies improve their competitiveness, driving up demand for Indian goods.
Corporate India, meanwhile, seems to be finally putting money into new buildings and factories.
India's gross fixed capital formation, which serves as a core indicator of total domestic public and private investment rose, nearly 12% in the first three months of this year.

"Non-government data also points to the fact that investment intentions of companies have gone up in recent months, with announcements especially concentrated in industries like data centres, renewable energy and metals," Madan Sabnavis, chief economist with the state-run Bank of Baroda, told the BBC.
"Of course, private investment is not broad-based yet, but these are definitely signs of a pick up."

stories.headline: A Congo Copper Mine Offers A Solar Plus Storage Playbook India's C&I Market Needs
stories.title: A Congo Copper Mine Offers A Solar Plus Storage Playbook India's C&I Market Needs
stories.summary: A solar-and-battery plant that opened this month near Kolwezi, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, is making a case that India's solar developers, DISCOMs and heavy industry should be paying close attention to: that firm, round-the-clock renewable power for a large industrial load is no longer a pilot-project curiosity. It is a bankable, fast-to-build alternative to the grid itself. The facility, developed, owned and financed by CrossBoundary Energy, pairs a 233 MWp solar array with a 123 MVA/526 MWh battery energy storage system to guarantee 30 MW of firm baseload power, around the clock, to Kamoa Copper S.A.'s mining complex. A joint venture between Ivanhoe Mines, Zijin Mining Group and the DRC government that runs Africa's largest copper operation. It reached commercial operation on August 12, just sixteen months after the power purchase agreement was signed in April 2025, against an African industry average of roughly 29 months for projects of similar scale. CrossBoundary says the plant is already outperforming its 30 MW guarantee, with the solar array delivering over 150 MW at peak and the surplus charging batteries for the night shift. Why CrossBoundary's Experience Matters To Indian solar As Well The commercial logic is the part worth studying. CrossBoundary says firm renewable electricity costs have fallen roughly 50% over five years, to the point that solar-plus-storage baseload is now cheaper than the diesel generators it replaces. Not cheaper on a subsidised, best-case basis, but cheaper on the economics a mine operator actually underwrites. That is precisely the argument India's open-access and captive-power segment has been building for large aluminium, cement, steel and textile consumers who have grown wary of DISCOM tariff unpredictability, cross-subsidy surcharges and curtailment risk. India already has the manufacturing base and BESS tendering pipeline to run this playbook at far larger scale than a single mine — Coal India's 187.5 MW/750 MWh BESS tender in Telangana and the steady drumbeat of C&I storage announcements from IESA's own market tracking are clear evidence the market exists. What the Kamoa project demonstrates is execution speed: a first-of-its-kind hybrid baseload system, procured, built and commissioned in industry-record time, for a customer with zero tolerance for downtime. Indian EPC contractors and battery integrators bidding for C&I and industrial-park storage work have a live benchmark to measure themselves against. Firm renewable electricity costs have fallen roughly 50% in five years — solar-plus-storage baseload is now demonstrably cheaper than the diesel gensets it replaces. The India read-through There is a supply-chain angle too. CrossBoundary's project used more than 350,000 solar modules and 90 BESS power conversion systems sourced through global tenders. Just the kind of large, time-bound procurement that Indian ALMM-listed module makers and the country's emerging BESS-pack assemblers are chasing as they look past a domestic market that remains tender-dependent and margin-thin. A fast-moving, creditworthy industrial buyer anywhere in the world is a reference customer worth having. None of this means India's DISCOM economics and Africa's off-grid mining logistics are directly comparable — India's grid is far more built out, and its C&I customers are optimising around tariffs and open-access charges rather than around diesel avoidance. But the direction of travel is the same: large power consumers increasingly prefer to own their supply security rather than negotiate it, and battery storage is what makes that ownership technically credible. For India's BESS tendering pipeline and its captive-power ambitions, Kamoa-Kakula is thus much more than a curiosity.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 3) suspended the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment imposed by the Delhi High Court on YouTuber Gulshan Pahuja for making videos scandalising the judiciary.
A bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu passed the order while issuing notice on Pahuja's appeal after hearing Advocate Manish.
The bench has ordered that the petitioner be released from custody immediately.
The High Court had initiated suo motu contempt against the YouTuber.
A division bench of Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja in May observed that Pahuja had shown “no regret” or “course correction” despite being found guilty of criminal contempt.

The High Court noted that during the hearing on sentence, Pahuja again made “scandalous remarks” against the judicial system, including statements that he expected no justice from Indian courts and likening judicial arbitrariness to “dictatorship”.

Pahuja had said that he expects no justice from the Indian judicial system and stated 'adaalaton ki manmarzi badhti jaa rahi hai aur main koi nyay ki umeed nahi kar raha' and also stated 'manmarzi ka dusra arth taanashahi hota hai'.
“The contemnor shows no regret for the same.
He also does not suggest any course correction,” the High Court observed, adding that he had in fact “compounds his contempt by making further scandalous submissions before this Court”.
The bench further said that failure to impose adequate punishment may “encourage him to repeat these acts in future and to embolden him in doing the same.”
Accordingly, the High Court imposed the “maximum punishment” of six months' simple imprisonment along with a fine of Rs.
2,000 in each contempt case, with sentences directed to run concurrently.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court refused to entertain a public interest litigation challenging the restrictions imposed by education authorities in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh on the entry of outsiders, journalists, YouTubers, social-media users and civil-society representatives into government schools, as well as curbs on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and livestreaming.
The petition filed by Priya Mishra was heard by a bench comprising Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe, which refused to entertain it.
"We are not inclined to entertain the writ petition filed under Article 32 of the Constitution of India."
The petition assumed significance in the wake of the “School Thik Karo” campaign being undertaken by the Cockroach Janat Party to expose the deficiencies in government school infrastructure.

It specifically challenged an August 16, 2026 circular issued by Rajasthan's Director of Secondary Education, which requires outsiders to obtain prior permission from the principal before entering the premises of government schools.
It also requires prior written permission for photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and livestreaming.

Regarding Uttar Pradesh, the petition refers to an August 19 order issued by the District Basic Education Officer, Ayodhya, directing that outsiders, YouTubers and persons associated with social media should not enter council schools or take photographs or videos without permission from the competent authority.
The petition states that similar directions were issued in several other districts, including Azamgarh, Ballia, Basti, Balrampur, Shamli and Agra.
The petitioner argued that the restrictions violate the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19(1)(a), 19(1)(g), 21 and 21-A of the Constitution.

It was contended that freedom of speech and expression encompasses legitimate journalism and dissemination of information concerning public institutions, while recognising that the State has a duty to protect children's privacy, dignity and safety.
The petitioner contended that there is a distinction between recording identifiable children and documenting the physical condition of a government school.

According to the petition, restrictions intended to protect children should not automatically prevent public-interest documentation of classrooms, buildings, toilets, drinking-water facilities, electricity, mid-day meals and other infrastructure.

article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday allowed Oil India Limited (OIL) to withdraw its interlocutory application challenging the Centre's refusal to approve its Extended Reach Drilling (ERD) project for extracting hydrocarbons beneath Assam's Dibru-Saikhowa National Park, with liberty to file a fresh petition.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order after senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, appearing for OIL, sought urgent hearing of the matter.
Dwivedi said the project was crucial to the country's energy requirements and involved drilling from outside the national park to reach hydrocarbon reserves located 3,500-4,000 metres underground.
He argued that ERD was not conventional mining and that the drilling infrastructure would remain outside the protected area.
OIL has challenged the Forest Advisory Committee's decision and the Environment Ministry's refusal to approve diversion of 0.069 hectares of forest land for the project.

The company contended that the authorities wrongly relied on the Supreme Court's 2023 order restricting mining in and around protected areas, and has also cited earlier orders permitting sub-surface hydrocarbon extraction beneath the park using ERD technology.

The company has also relied on earlier orders of the top court in 2017, when it was permitted, subject to conditions and safeguards, to extract hydrocarbons beneath the national park using ERD technology.

It said the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife had recommended the proposal and that the top court subsequently allowed sub-surface hydrocarbon extraction, subject to compliance with environmental and wildlife protection conditions.
It sought to set aside the order of August 02, 2024 passed by the MoEFCC and also the minutes of the meeting of the Forest Advisory Committee of the MoEFCC on July 4, 2024.

stories.title: ICICI Bank acquires 2% stake from joint venture partner of its life insurance arm for ₹1,470 cr
stories.summary: The bank's shareholding in ICICI Life stands at approximately 52.8%

article_sentences: ICICI Bank on Wednesday said it has raised its stake in its life insurance venture by buying a 2 per cent stake from its joint venture partner for a sum of ₹1,470 crore.

The bank has, through multiple tranches executed between July 22 and September 2, 2026, completed the purchase of 29,015,693 equity shares of ICICI Life, representing about 2 per cent of ICICI Life's equity share capital on June 30, 2026, for an approximate consideration of Rs 14.70 billion through the stock exchange mechanism, ICICI Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Following this, the bank's shareholding in ICICI Life stands at approximately 52.8 per cent.
Paring down of stake by its joint venture partner, UK-based Prudential plc, is part of regulatory requirement.
Prudential plc announced its plans in May this year to acquire a 75 per cent stake in Bharti Life Insurance.
According to the regulatory requirement, Prudential plc has to reduce its stake in ICICI Prudential Life Insurance to 10 per cent before increasing its holding in Bharti Life Insurance.
Prior to the stake sale, Prudential plc's holding in ICICI Life Insurance was 21.9 per cent, while ICICI Bank had a 50.9 per cent majority stake.

stories.headline: Lal Chowk protest reflects public anger: LoP Sharma
stories.title: Lal Chowk protest reflects public anger: LoP Sharma
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 2: Leader of Opposition in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly Sunil Sharma on Wednesday said the protest march at Lal Chowk towards the Civil Secretariat reflected growing public anger over what he termed the National Conference government’s failures, unfulfilled promises and lack of transparency. Sharma said people across Jammu and Kashmir, particularly the youth, were seeking answers on unemployment, electricity tariffs, recruitment and promises made by the National Conference ahead of the 2024 Assembly elections. He questioned the government over its election commitments, including 200 units of free electricity, an end to smart meters, 10 kg of ration and one lakh jobs. “The people of J&K want to know—where are these promises?” Sharma said, alleging that the government had failed to deliver on commitments made to voters. The BJP leader also raised concerns over the engagement of thousands of people through outsourcing. Referring to discussions in the Assembly, he said the Chief Minister had spoken about the engagement of around 20,000–25,000 people through outsourcing. Sharma sought clarity on the recruitment mechanism and asked whether such positions would be advertised and opened to all eligible candidates through a transparent, merit-based process. He alleged that government employment should not become a means of political favouritism or backdoor appointments and called for equal opportunities for all eligible candidates. Sharma said the BJP would continue to raise issues concerning employment, recruitment, electricity, development and governance both inside and outside the Assembly. “The message from Lal Chowk is clear: the people want jobs, merit, transparency, development and accountability,” he said. He further urged the government to honour its commitments and provide answers on the promises made to the people during the election campaign.

stories.headline: Agriculture sector provides 70% of livelihoods, contributes 18% to J&K GDP: Government
stories.title: Agriculture sector provides 70% of livelihoods, contributes 18% to J&K GDP: Government
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 2: Agriculture and allied activities provide around 70 per cent of livelihoods in Jammu and Kashmir and contribute about 18 per cent to the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), the official figures have revealed. As per the government statistics highlighting the agriculture sector’s progress between 2019-20 and 2025-26, the government has listed a series of achievements in the agriculture and allied sectors, including a more than two-fold increase in cold storage capacity, expansion of crop insurance, growth in milk and fish production and increased horticulture exports. As per the figures, cold storage capacity in J&K increased from 1.39 lakh metric tonnes to 2.97 lakh MT from 2019-20 to 2025-26. Under the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, Rs 4,383.61 crore has been disbursed to 9,16,587 lakh farmers, the document states. The government figures presented before the recently convened meeting with Niti Aayog members, the government said two Horticulture Centres of excellence and one Agriculture Centre of Excellence have been established, while 13 others are under execution. “The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana has also been extended to all 20 districts,” the official document reads. The government claimed that the Kisan Credit Card scheme has 11.44 lakh active cards, with Rs 10,964 crore in loans sanctioned. “Milk processing capacity increased seven-fold, from 35,000 litres to 2.50 lakh litres per day, while fish production rose by 40 per cent from 21,000 MT to 31,700 MT,” the official document reads. As per the official statistics, seven agricultural products have received Geographical Indication (GI) tags, with 20 more products under process. “The National Agriculture Market has linked 17 mandis and registered 2,750 traders since 2019,” the official document reads. The government claimed that Horticulture exports also increased from 11.87 lakh MT in 2020-21 to 13.86 lakh MT in 2025-26. In the meeting, the government also highlighted progress under the Holistic Agriculture Development Programme (HADP), including the establishment of 1.46 lakh units and generation of 4 crore person-days of employment. “Under area expansion initiatives, 12,764 hectares have been brought under crops including Mushqbudji rice, red rice, chilli, hill garlic and vegetables,” the official document reads. The government informed the Niti Aayog team that 2.88 lakh farmers have been skilled through the DAKSH KISAN initiative. The document reads that mushroom production increased from 2,100 MT in 2021-22 to 3,765 MT, while honey production rose from 2,200 MT to 3,900 MT. The seed replacement rate has increased from 12 per cent to 20 per cent, while 1,150 saffron and 890 other nurseries have been registered. As per the official statistics, a total of 1,807 KissanKhidmatGhars have been established, with 9.41 lakh farmers registered and 5.2 lakh farms geo-tagged and on boarded. The HADP progress also includes the establishment of 481 Hi-Tech Poly Greenhouses covering 2.26 lakh square metres and 966 low-cost poly greenhouses covering 2.18 lakh square metres. As per the official data, under the Yellow Revolution, the area under oilseed cultivation has expanded from 1.40 lakh hectares. The document also outlines the Competitiveness Improvement of Agriculture and Allied Project (JK-CIP), a $217 million (approximately Rs 1,800 crore) project focused on improving the climate and market ecosystem across 90 blocks. The project targets marginal communities and women and is expected to benefit around three lakh households, or approximately 15 lakh people. “Its components include climate-smart and market-led production, development support for the agri-business ecosystem, and support to vulnerable communities and project management,” the document reads. The expected outcomes after seven years include scaling up collectivisation, strengthening and establishing Farmer Producer Organisations, supporting business-led enterprises, market support and brand development, assistance to startups and benefits to three lakh households. The government claimed that under JK-CIP, 65,123 farmers have been registered and 73,472 applications have been received so far. “Of these, 18,046 applications are under process, while 48,348 have been approved. A total of 9,131 units have been established,” the document reads. The document also mentioned the proposed introduction of a restructured Weather-Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) for fruit crops, including apple, saffron, litchi and mango. “The fresh tendering process for the scheme will be initiated after issuance of the revised RWBCIS operational guidelines by the Government of India,” the document reads.
